title: Jeremiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 26.

questions.question: At the beginning of whose reign did the word from the LORD come to Jeremiah?
options: Jehoiakim
Josiah
Hezekiah
Urijah
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoiakim
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:1 states that the word came in the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah.

questions.question: Where was Jeremiah commanded by the LORD to stand and speak to the cities of Judah?
options: In the court of the LORD'S house
On the city walls
In the king's palace
At the city gate
questions.correctAnswer: In the court of the LORD'S house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:2 directs Jeremiah to stand in the court of the LORD'S house and speak to all the cities of Judah.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah commanded not to do with the words the LORD gave him?
options: Diminish not a word
Make them easier to understand
Add his own interpretation
Speak only to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Diminish not a word
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:2 commands Jeremiah to speak all the words that the LORD commanded and to diminish not a word.

questions.question: What condition would cause the LORD to repent of the evil He purposed to do?
options: If they hearken and turn every man from his evil way
If they offer more sacrifices
If they build a new temple
If they appoint new priests
questions.correctAnswer: If they hearken and turn every man from his evil way
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:3 says the LORD would repent if they hearken and turn from their evil way.

questions.question: According to the LORD, what would happen if the people refuse to hearken and walk in His law?
options: He will make the house like Shiloh and the city a curse
He will bless the city
He will send more prophets
He will build a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: He will make the house like Shiloh and the city a curse
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:6 states that if they do not hearken, the LORD will make the house like Shiloh and the city a curse.

questions.question: Who heard Jeremiah speaking the words in the house of the LORD?
options: The priests, the prophets, and all the people
Only the priests
Only the king and princes
Foreign emissaries
questions.correctAnswer: The priests, the prophets, and all the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:7 says that the priests, prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking in the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the priests, prophets, and people after Jeremiah finished speaking?
options: They said he should surely die
They praised him
They ignored him
They asked for more prophecies
questions.correctAnswer: They said he should surely die
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:8 records that after Jeremiah finished speaking, the priests and prophets and all the people said he should surely die.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was commanded to only speak to the priests and prophets in the LORD'S house.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:2 commands him to speak to all the cities of Judah that come to worship in the LORD'S house, not only to priests and prophets.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah warned that if the people put him to death, they would bring innocent blood upon themselves.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:15 states that if they put Jeremiah to death, they would bring innocent blood upon themselves and the city.

questions.question: Who came from the king's house to the house of the LORD upon hearing the accusations against Jeremiah?
options: The princes of Judah
The priests only
The prophets only
Foreign ambassadors
questions.correctAnswer: The princes of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:10 says the princes of Judah came from the king's house to the house of the LORD after hearing the accusations.

questions.question: What was the accusation against Jeremiah by the priests and prophets?
options: He prophesied that the house would be like Shiloh and the city desolate
He stole from the temple
He allied with the enemies
He refused to speak
questions.correctAnswer: He prophesied that the house would be like Shiloh and the city desolate
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:9-11 show they accused Jeremiah of prophesying that the house would be like Shiloh and the city desolate without inhabitant.

questions.question: Who protected Jeremiah from being handed over to the people to be put to death?
options: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
Jehoiakim the king
Urijah the son of Shemaiah
Micah the Morasthite
questions.correctAnswer: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:24 states that the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah to prevent his death.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah told the people to obey the LORD their God so that He would repent of the evil pronounced against them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:13 records Jeremiah urging the people to amend their ways and obey the LORD so He might repent of the evil.

questions.question: Which of these events happened first in Jeremiah 26?
options: Jeremiah speaks in the LORD'S house
The people accuse Jeremiah and want him put to death
The princes come to hear the case
Ahikam protects Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah speaks in the LORD'S house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:7 shows Jeremiah speaking in the LORD'S house first, before the accusations and other events.

questions.question: True or False: The priests and prophets immediately agreed Jeremiah was not worthy to die after he spoke.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:8-11 show the priests and prophets initially said Jeremiah should die for his prophecy.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the priests, prophets, and all the people when Jeremiah finished speaking the words commanded by the LORD?
options: They praised him for his courage
They took him and said he must surely die
They ignored his words and left the temple
They asked him to explain further
questions.correctAnswer: They took him and said he must surely die
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:8 shows that after Jeremiah finished speaking, the priests, prophets, and all the people took him and said he must surely die, as they opposed his prophecy.

questions.question: Why did the people gather against Jeremiah in the house of the LORD?
options: Because he prophesied peace and prosperity
Because he prophesied destruction and desolation for the city
Because he refused to speak in the temple
Because he criticized the priests and prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Because he prophesied destruction and desolation for the city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:9 explains that the people gathered against Jeremiah because he prophesied that the house would be like Shiloh and the city would be desolate without inhabitants.

questions.question: Where did the princes of Judah sit when they came to hear about Jeremiah's prophecy?
options: In the king's throne room
In the entry of the new gate of the LORD's house
In the marketplace outside the city
In the high priest's chamber
questions.correctAnswer: In the entry of the new gate of the LORD's house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:10 states that the princes came from the king's house and sat down in the entry of the new gate of the LORD's house to listen to the accusations and Jeremiah's defense.

questions.question: What accusation did the priests and prophets make against Jeremiah before the princes and all the people?
options: He had stolen from the temple
He was worthy to die for prophesying against the city
He was teaching false doctrine
He was not a true prophet
questions.correctAnswer: He was worthy to die for prophesying against the city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:11 records that the priests and prophets declared Jeremiah worthy to die because he had prophesied against the city as heard by all.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah respond to the accusations against him in Jeremiah 26:12-13?
options: He denies ever prophesying against the city
He claims the LORD sent him to warn and calls the people to amend their ways
He calls for the people to arrest the priests
He declares the city is already doomed and cannot be saved
questions.correctAnswer: He claims the LORD sent him to warn and calls the people to amend their ways
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 26:12-13, Jeremiah says the LORD sent him to prophesy against the city, urging the people to amend their ways and obey God, so that the LORD may repent of the evil pronounced.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah say will happen if the people put him to death, according to Jeremiah 26:15?
options: They will be blessed by God
They will bring innocent blood upon themselves and the city
They will be forgiven for their sins
They will receive peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: They will bring innocent blood upon themselves and the city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:15 warns that putting Jeremiah to death will bring innocent blood upon the people, the city, and its inhabitants because the LORD truly sent Jeremiah to speak these words.

questions.question: What decision did the princes and all the people make about Jeremiah's life after hearing his defense?
options: They decided to imprison him
They decided he was not worthy to die
They decided to exile him
They decided to ignore his prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: They decided he was not worthy to die
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:16 records that the princes and all the people told the priests and prophets that Jeremiah was not worthy to die because he spoke in the name of the LORD.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 26:17-19, what example is given to encourage not killing Jeremiah?
options: The story of Elijah's miracles
The prophecy of Micah in Hezekiah's days and the mercy shown then
The exile of Daniel in Babylon
The building of Solomon's temple
questions.correctAnswer: The prophecy of Micah in Hezekiah's days and the mercy shown then
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:18-19 recount the example of Micah's prophecy during Hezekiah's reign, where the king and Judah did not kill the prophet but feared the LORD and sought Him, leading to God repenting of the evil pronounced.

questions.question: What happened to Urijah the son of Shemaiah after he prophesied against the city, according to Jeremiah 26:20-23?
options: He was honored by the king
He was ignored and remained safe
He fled to Egypt but was brought back and killed by the king
He was protected by the priests
questions.correctAnswer: He fled to Egypt but was brought back and killed by the king
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:21-23 tells that Urijah fled to Egypt fearing death, but King Jehoiakim sent men to bring him back, and the king killed him and cast his body into the graves of the common people.

questions.question: Who protected Jeremiah from being handed over to the people to be put to death, as stated in Jeremiah 26:24?
options: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
King Jehoiakim
The priests and prophets
The princes of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:24 shows that Ahikam the son of Shaphan used his influence to protect Jeremiah from being given into the hands of the people to be put to death.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah boldly accepts his fate and tells the people to do to him as they see fit.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:14 records Jeremiah saying he is in their hand and they may do to him as they see good and meet, showing his submission to God's will through the people's decision.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah assures the people that if they amend their ways and obey God, He will not bring the evil He pronounced upon them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:13 promises that if the people amend their ways and obey the voice of the LORD, He will repent of the evil pronounced against them.

questions.question: True or False: The priests and prophets agreed with Jeremiah and supported his prophecy from the beginning.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:11 shows that the priests and prophets accused Jeremiah as worthy to die for prophesying against the city, indicating their opposition rather than support.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 26:15-16, how did the princes and people reconcile Jeremiah's prophecy with their judgment about his life?
options: They believed Jeremiah was lying and wanted him punished
They acknowledged he spoke in God's name and decided he should not die
They ignored his prophecy and focused on his behavior
They deferred the decision to the king
questions.correctAnswer: They acknowledged he spoke in God's name and decided he should not die
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:15-16 shows that despite Jeremiah's warning about innocent blood, the princes and people recognized he spoke in the LORD's name and concluded he was not worthy to die.

questions.question: What lesson about obedience and consequences can a believer learn from Jeremiah 26:4-6?
options: Ignoring God's law leads to destruction of the temple and city
Obedience is optional and does not affect the nation
Prophets are not important in guiding the people
God does not send warnings through His servants
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring God's law leads to destruction of the temple and city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:4-6 states that if the people do not heed God's law and the prophets, God will make the house like Shiloh and the city a curse, teaching the serious consequences of disobedience.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 26.

questions.question: Who defended Jeremiah by reminding the assembly about Micah's prophecy during King Hezekiah's reign?
options: Certain elders of the land
The priests and prophets
King Jehoiakim himself
The people of Kirjathjearim
questions.correctAnswer: Certain elders of the land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:17 records that certain elders rose up and spoke to defend Jeremiah by citing Micah's prophecy in Hezekiah's days.

questions.question: What was the consequence Micah prophesied for Zion and Jerusalem in the days of Hezekiah?
options: Zion would flourish and Jerusalem would be rebuilt
Zion would be plowed like a field and Jerusalem become heaps
Zion would be covered with gold and Jerusalem become a capital
Zion and Jerusalem would be untouched
questions.correctAnswer: Zion would be plowed like a field and Jerusalem become heaps
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:18 states that Micah prophesied that Zion would be plowed like a field and Jerusalem become heaps, symbolizing desolation.

questions.question: What did the elders say was the reason Hezekiah and Judah did not kill Micah after his prophecy?
options: They did not hear the prophecy
They feared the LORD and besought Him to repent
They agreed with the prophecy and welcomed it
They had no power to kill him
questions.correctAnswer: They feared the LORD and besought Him to repent
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:19 explains that Hezekiah and Judah feared the LORD and pleaded with Him, resulting in the LORD repenting of the evil He had pronounced.

questions.question: Who was Urijah and what happened to him after he prophesied against Jerusalem and Judah?
options: A priest who was promoted after his prophecy
A prophet who fled to Egypt but was brought back and killed
A king who repented after hearing Jeremiah
A scribe who recorded Jeremiah's words
questions.correctAnswer: A prophet who fled to Egypt but was brought back and killed
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:20-23 recounts that Urijah prophesied like Jeremiah, fled to Egypt when threatened, was brought back by Jehoiakim's men, and was killed.

questions.question: Which figure protected Jeremiah from being handed over to the people for death?
options: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
King Josiah
The priests of the LORD's house
The elders of the land
questions.correctAnswer: Ahikam the son of Shaphan
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:24 states that the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, preventing the people from putting him to death.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'repent' (used in Jeremiah 26:3 and 26:19) primarily convey in the context of this chapter?
options: To feel sorry without changing behavior
To change one's mind and turn away from evil
To punish someone severely
To forget past sins
questions.correctAnswer: To change one's mind and turn away from evil
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 26:3 and 26:19, 'repent' (Hebrew 'nacham') means God changing His planned judgment if the people turn from their evil ways.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Jeremiah 26:6 where the LORD says He will make the house like Shiloh and the city a curse to all nations?
options: Simile
Hyperbole
Personification
Paradox
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:6 uses a simile comparing the LORD's judgment on the temple and city to Shiloh's ruin, illustrating desolation.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah warned that if he was killed, innocent blood would be upon the people and the city.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:15 clearly states that if they put Jeremiah to death, they would bring innocent blood upon themselves and the city.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoiakim respected Urijah’s prophecy and allowed him to live in peace.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:21-23 shows Jehoiakim sought to kill Urijah, who fled but was captured and slain by the king’s orders.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament prophet’s experience does Jeremiah 26:19 recall to persuade the people not to kill Jeremiah?
options: Isaiah
Micah
Elijah
Jonah
questions.correctAnswer: Micah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:19 recalls Micah’s prophecy and how King Hezekiah did not kill him, urging the people to avoid similar sin.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 26:12-13, what must the people do to cause the LORD to repent of the evil He has pronounced against them?
options: Offer sacrifices in the LORD's house
Amend their ways and obey the voice of the LORD
Build a larger temple
Send gifts to the priests and prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Amend their ways and obey the voice of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:13 instructs the people to amend their ways and obey the LORD’s voice so He may repent of the evil pronounced.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah respond to the threat of death according to Jeremiah 26:14-15?
options: He begs for his life to be spared
He proclaims he will escape by flight
He accepts his fate but warns of innocent blood guilt
He curses those who threaten him
questions.correctAnswer: He accepts his fate but warns of innocent blood guilt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:14-15 shows Jeremiah submits to their will but warns that killing him would bring guilt of innocent blood.

questions.question: What historical-cultural context is reflected in the elders’ reference to Micah’s prophecy in Jeremiah 26:18-19?
options: The common practice of executing prophets who predicted disaster
The tradition of kings forgiving all prophets
The lack of any previous prophetic warnings
The alliance between Judah and Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The common practice of executing prophets who predicted disaster
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:18-19 reflects the cultural reality that prophets predicting disaster risked death but Hezekiah’s fear of God prevented it.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of innocent blood guilt present in Jeremiah 26:15?
options: Matthew 23:35
Acts 2:38
Romans 3:23
Hebrews 11:1
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 23:35
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:35 speaks of the blood of righteous Abel and prophets shed on earth, echoing Jeremiah’s warning about innocent blood guilt (Jeremiah 26:15).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 26:24 suggest about the role of political allies in protecting prophets from persecution in ancient Judah?
options: They had no influence over the people
They could intervene and prevent death sentences
They often betrayed prophets for political gain
They were powerless against royal decrees
questions.correctAnswer: They could intervene and prevent death sentences
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:24 shows Ahikam the son of Shaphan’s hand was with Jeremiah, indicating political allies could protect prophets from persecution.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the primary command God gives to Jeremiah at the beginning of his prophecy in Jeremiah 26?
options: Stand in the court of the LORD's house and speak all the words God commands without diminishing any word
Only warn the priests and prophets about their sins
Speak only to the king and his princes about Judah's future
Preach repentance only if the people ask for it
questions.correctAnswer: Stand in the court of the LORD's house and speak all the words God commands without diminishing any word
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:2 commands Jeremiah to stand in the court of the LORD's house and speak to all the cities of Judah all the words God commands, without diminishing any word, emphasizing the completeness and authority of the prophetic message.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by God's willingness to 'repent' of the evil He plans to do if the people turn from their evil ways?
options: Omniscience
Immutability
Mercy
Justice
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:3 reveals God's merciful attribute, showing that He is willing to relent or 'repent' of the evil He planned if the people genuinely turn away from their evil, highlighting His patience and compassion.

questions.question: What consequence does God declare for the house of the LORD and Jerusalem if the people refuse to obey His law and the prophets?
options: They will be blessed above all nations
They will be made like Shiloh and become a curse to all nations
They will receive immediate destruction by fire
They will be spared but lose their king
questions.correctAnswer: They will be made like Shiloh and become a curse to all nations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:6 states that if the people do not obey, God will make the house like Shiloh (a place that lost its sacred status) and make Jerusalem a curse to all nations, emphasizing judgment for disobedience.

questions.question: How did the priests, prophets, and people react to Jeremiah's prophecy about the destruction of the house and city?
options: They rejoiced and repented immediately
They took him and said he must surely die
They ignored his words completely
They asked the king to protect Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: They took him and said he must surely die
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:8 records that after Jeremiah finished prophesying, the priests, prophets, and people seized him, demanding his death because of the threatening prophecy against the temple and city.

questions.question: What rationale did the priests and prophets give to the princes and people for wanting Jeremiah put to death?
options: He had stolen from the temple treasury
He had prophesied against the city and temple, causing fear
He refused to perform priestly duties
He was conspiring with foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: He had prophesied against the city and temple, causing fear
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:11 explains that the priests and prophets declared Jeremiah worthy of death because he prophesied against the city, which alarmed the people and leaders.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by Jeremiah's statement that if they kill him, they will bring innocent blood upon themselves and the city?
options: The doctrine of substitutionary atonement
The doctrine of human responsibility and guilt for sin
The doctrine of election
The doctrine of sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of human responsibility and guilt for sin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:15 emphasizes that killing a prophet sent by God brings guilt and innocent bloodshed upon the people, underscoring human accountability for rejecting God's messengers and commands.

questions.question: Which figure from earlier Judahite history is cited by the elders to argue that a prophet's harsh judgment does not necessarily result in death but repentance from God?
options: Isaiah the prophet
Micah the Morasthite
Elijah the Tishbite
Daniel the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: Micah the Morasthite
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:18 references Micah the Morasthite, who prophesied similar destruction, but was not put to death because King Hezekiah and Judah feared God and repented, showing God's mercy.

questions.question: What happened to Urijah the prophet after he fled to Egypt, and what does this reveal about the king's attitude towards prophetic warnings?
options: He was honored as a wise man
He was brought back and killed by King Jehoiakim
He was allowed to live in exile
He was appointed a royal advisor
questions.correctAnswer: He was brought back and killed by King Jehoiakim
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:23 describes how Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt to bring back Urijah, who was then slain by the king, showing Jehoiakim's hostility to prophets delivering God's judgment.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by His sending multiple prophets repeatedly to warn Judah as stated in Jeremiah 26?
options: God's omnipotence
God's patience and long-suffering
God's wrath
God's sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: God's patience and long-suffering
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:5 mentions God sending prophets early and often, indicating His patience and desire for repentance before judgment, highlighting His longsuffering nature.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 26:12-13 together teach about the possibility of repentance and God's response to human obedience?
options: Repentance is impossible once judgment is declared
Obedience to God's voice can lead God to repent of evil pronounced
God will punish regardless of human actions
Only kings can change God's mind
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's voice can lead God to repent of evil pronounced
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:12-13 shows Jeremiah calling the people to amend their ways and obey God, assuring that then God will relent of the evil He pronounced, teaching the doctrine of conditional divine judgment.

questions.question: What does the protection of Jeremiah by Ahikam son of Shaphan in Jeremiah 26 signify about divine providence and human agency?
options: Human power always overrides divine will
God providentially uses faithful individuals to preserve His servants
Prophets are always protected by kings
Protection is guaranteed by the temple priests
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially uses faithful individuals to preserve His servants
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:24 shows that Ahikam's hand was with Jeremiah to save him from death, illustrating how God's providence can work through faithful people to fulfill His purposes.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that prophecy in the Old Testament is often ignored or results in the death of the prophet, thus disproving God's justice and mercy. What does Jeremiah 26:16-19 actually teach about God's justice and mercy in relation to prophetic warnings?
options: God always punishes prophets who speak harsh truths
God uses prophetic warnings to call for repentance and shows mercy if people respond
Prophetic death is proof God is unjust
Prophets have no real authority
questions.correctAnswer: God uses prophetic warnings to call for repentance and shows mercy if people respond
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:16-19 presents a case where elders remind the assembly that previous prophets like Micah were not killed because of repentance and God's mercy, teaching that God's justice includes calls to repentance and the opportunity for mercy.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 26:1-6 combined with 26:20-23 illustrate the conflict between divine sovereignty and human opposition in the prophetic mission?
options: God's sovereign plan is thwarted by kings and princes
Prophets have no divine authority
Despite human hostility, God's sovereign plan to warn and judge is fulfilled through prophets like Jeremiah and Urijah
Prophetic messages depend solely on the king's approval
questions.correctAnswer: Despite human hostility, God's sovereign plan to warn and judge is fulfilled through prophets like Jeremiah and Urijah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:1-6 shows God's command to Jeremiah to warn the people, while 26:20-23 recounts how another prophet Urijah was killed for a similar message, indicating that although human opposition exists, God's sovereign purpose through prophecy persists.

questions.question: What doctrine is underscored by the people's initial impulse to kill Jeremiah for his prophecy, contrasted with the princes and elders deciding he should live because he spoke in God's name?
options: The doctrine of divine election
The doctrine of the authority of prophetic revelation and human discernment
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of the priesthood of all believers
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the authority of prophetic revelation and human discernment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:8-16 shows the tension between rejecting and accepting prophetic words, teaching that while human response varies, the authority of God's revelation through prophets must be discerned and respected.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 26 illustrate the theme of covenantal accountability in the relationship between God and Judah?
options: God ignores Judah's sins
Judah is accountable to God to obey His law and heed His prophets or face judgment
The covenant allows Judah to sin without consequence
Prophets have no role in covenant enforcement
questions.correctAnswer: Judah is accountable to God to obey His law and heed His prophets or face judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 26:4-6 and 12-13 show God warning Judah to obey His law and listen to His prophets, linking obedience with blessing and disobedience with punishment, underscoring covenantal accountability.
